notes: The federation's own first newsgroup post: a five-match debut card, Saturday Night Live, billed for the following night.

name: EMWO Tuesday Terror, 23 June 1998

date.source: The document's own live dateline (U.S. Arena, Washington, D.C.).

matches.note: Destroyer won at 6:21 with the Destroyer Bomb after a masked ally's chair shot on Johnson went unseen by the referee.
York won at 4:54, using a hidden glass bottle and a pair of brass knuckles before finishing with his own Class Act.
Vars won the main event at 16:40, putting Harrison through two tables and finishing with a top-rope piledriver, the varSDrop.

no_appearances_reason: A tag-team opener (Element of Pain vs. the JoA) is not minted -- its four wrestlers are recorded only in the served broadcast's own text.
notes: The federation's own second Tuesday Terror: a cold open on two upcoming title contenders, a backstage segment with President "Confident" Lawrence Williams naming the card, a tag-team debut, and a hardcore main event.

name: EMWO Independence Day Decimation, 4 July 1998

date.source: The card's own dateline (Pittsburgh Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania).

no_appearances_reason: Full match-by-match structuring is deferred; this document is the fed's own final lineup, not a results report, and the one confirmed outcome recovered from a later recap (Christian York over Destroyer by run-in) is recorded in this show's own notes rather than as a match record.
notes: A free two-hour special, billed by the promotion as bigger than its regular weekly shows: a no-disqualifications main event pairing the Godfather and a former rival federation's own Heavyweight Champion, Derek Douglas; a Hell in a Cell bout; and a tournament eliminator in which the returning "Flamboyant" Paul Dare cost Destroyer his match against "Mr. Charisma" Christian York, sending York on to a vacant-title match at the promotion's own first pay-per-view, Summer Sizzler.

name: EMWO Tuesday Terror, 21 July 1998

date.source: The document's own live dateline; broadcast across the Miami Arena and the Reunion Arena, Dallas.

matches.note: Norman won his and Harvey's shared federation debut at 10:24 with his own LethalSlam.
Alexander won his own federation debut at 7:39 with a top-rope DDT after repeated chair shots; the broadcast's own announcers call it Mott's retirement from wrestling the same night.
Kabukii won his own federation debut at 7:33 with the Bonzaii Guillotine Leg Drop.
Dare won his own federation debut at 10:39 with his own finisher, the Market Crash, in what the broadcast bills as Johnson's own final EMWO match.

notes: Four debut singles matches broadcast from two arenas; between matches, co-host "Bad Boy" Bruce Bingham books his own in-ring return against a broadcast rival for the promotion's own first pay-per-view, Summer Sizzler.

name: EMWO Special Report, 2 September 1998
no_appearances_reason: A staged in-fiction newscast, not a match or a results report; its named figures (the president and the closing-storyline antagonist) are recorded in this wing's own registry rather than as billed appearances on this document.
notes: A staged in-fiction newscast folding the federation's real closing into its own storyline: President Lawrence Williams blames a lawsuit for the shutdown, and "Homeless" Joe Boxcar answers with a career-stakes challenge for the promotion's own closing pay-per-view, Grand Finale.
